newsitem.title: INDIA: India's STC confirms one mln tonne wheat purchase.
newsitem.headline: India's STC confirms one mln tonne wheat purchase.

text.p: India's state-run State Trading Corp (STC) confirmed on Friday that it had bought one million tonnes of wheat from Australia for delivery starting in January.
"We have bought one million tonnes," a senior STC official who did not want to be identified told Reuters.
The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Friday it had sold one million tonnes of Australian Standard White wheat to India for January-February delivery at a price of around A$185 a tonne, FOB.
The STC official confirmed the price.

Food Minister Devendra Prasad Yadav told parliament on Thursday that India will import two million tonnes of wheat in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) to increase domestic supplies and check rising prices.
The official said STC would be responsible for importing the entire two million tonnes.
He said the one-million-tonne purchase was made over the past few days, and bought in lots of 50,000 tonnes.
The official said STC would float a global tender for more wheat purchases but gave no other details.
"The process has started. We still have to cover the remaining one million," he said.
He said Argentina, the United States, Canada and the European Union could be potential markets.
A special cell has been set up at STC to handle the wheat imports, he said.
The official said the imported wheat would be used to build a buffer.
"The whole idea is to draw out the hoarded wheat. It (hoarded stock) could be four million tonnes," the official said.
Traders said this week that dwindling government reserves had caused wheat prices to rise sharply in recent months compared with prices last year.
Earlier analysts had said that even without imports, domestic prices were expected to start to fall in February since the new crop was due in March.
India expects a wheat crop of about 64 million tonnes in calendar 1997. A clear picture should emerge by early February.
Government wheat procurement in the 1995/96 (July-June) growing season fell to 8.2 million tonnes from 12.3 million the previous year due to a three-million-tonne shortfall in output.
As of October 1, the state-run Food Corporation of India held 19.6 million tonnes of foodgrain -- wheat, rice and other cereals -- down from 29.9 million a year earlier.

India last imported wheat in 1991/92 (April-March), when it bought two million tonnes. It exported 600,000 tonnes in 1995/96 and 1.07 million tonnes in 1996/97 up to September 30 this year, when the government halted exports.
-- Hari Ramachandran, New Delhi newsroom +91 11 301 2024
